channel.title: Banks & NBFCs · Market Pressure Map
channel.description: Daily news scored for its impact on Banks & NBFCs in Indian markets. Today: mixed (+0.7).

item.title: [−1] US 10-year Treasury yield hovers near 5.3%, its highest since 2002
item.description:
The 10-year yield touched a fresh 2002 high to start the week before easing to about 5.26%. It has risen about 0.46 points in a month. Ongoing.

Banks & NBFCs: mild headwind (−1) — Foreign selling in lenders

Why it matters: High US yields draw foreign money out of Indian stocks and bonds, weaken the rupee and push up Indian bond yields.

Market gauges: Foreign investor flows −2, Rupee −1, Bond market (G-Secs) −1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: [+1] India's services PMI rises to 55.2 in September, a three-month high, as input cost inflation eases
item.description:
The final services PMI was 55.2, up from 54.1 but below the 55.8 flash and 56.2 expected. New business rose fastest in three months; input cost inflation fell to a 10-month low. New.

Banks & NBFCs: mild tailwind (+1) — Demand firmer in financial services

Why it matters: Firmer services demand supports earnings and jobs, while easing cost pressure helps the inflation outlook ahead of the RBI decision.

Market gauges: Growth outlook +1, Inflation outlook +1

Confidence: high · horizon: weeks

item.title: [+1] RBI rate panel in day two; decision due October 7 with a 25 bps hike to 5.50% widely expected
item.description:
The MPC concludes tomorrow. Most economists expect the first hike since February 2023, from 5.25%. The 10-year G-Sec yield stood at 7.21% on October 5. Ongoing: expectations unchanged since last week.

Banks & NBFCs: mild tailwind (+1) — Lending margins widen at first

Why it matters: A hike is largely priced; the statement on further tightening and the inflation forecast will move bond yields, the rupee and rate-sensitive sectors such as housing and autos.

Market gauges: Bond market (G-Secs) −2, Growth outlook −1, Rupee +1

Confidence: medium · horizon: weeks
